original_question: For a holomorphic foliation on complex projective space, possibly with singularities, must every leaf accumulate at a singular point of the foliation?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.1, the paper’s “Exceptional minimal set problem,” which is the formal version of the introduction’s question “Do leaves always cluster at singular points?” specialized to foliations on the complex projective plane. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core issue: a holomorphic foliation with singularities, and the question whether every leaf must approach or accumulate on a singular point. It also correctly uses a universal quantifier over leaves, which matches the paper’s official problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: The paper formulates the problem on the complex projective plane P^2(C), not on an arbitrary complex projective space P^n(C). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The notation in the paper fixes a holomorphic foliation F and its finite singular set Sing(F). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The paper does not phrase the issue informally as “accumulate”; it asks whether, for every leaf L of F, the closure of L intersects Sing(F). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The leaves under discussion are the leaves of the foliation on P^2(C) minus Sing(F). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Problem 5.1 includes no extra hypotheses on degree, genericity, or hyperbolicity; adding such restrictions would move away from the paper’s exact scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
The paper presents this as a specific open problem in Section 5, not as a higher-dimensional projective-space variant. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on the complex projective plane P^2(C), and let Sing(F) denote its finite singular set. If L is any leaf of F in P^2(C) minus Sing(F), must the closure of L in P^2(C) intersect Sing(F)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The introduction lists “Do leaves always cluster at singular points?” as one of the paper’s motivating open questions, and Section 5 then gives the exact formal statement as Problem 5.1 for a holomorphic foliation F on P^2 with finite singular set Sing(F): whether every leaf has closure meeting Sing(F). The paragraph immediately after Problem 5.1 supplies the nearby context: the question is attributed to Camacho–Lins Neto–Sad, and the answer is known to be positive when F admits a directed positive closed current, in particular when F has an invariant algebraic curve. This confirms that your draft is aimed at Problem 5.1, but it is broader than the paper because it replaces P^2 by general projective space and leaves the closure condition implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
